title: The Founder's Mindset: Making Ideas Happen
about:
A keynote-driven course from The Platform Nigeria, taught by Vusi Thembekwayo, globally acclaimed entrepreneur and venture capitalist. The whole course rests on one idea: it is not about ideas, it is about making ideas happen.

You will move from inspiration to execution, understand the scale of the opportunity in front of you, and learn the four things founders do to build businesses that outgrow them.
benefits:
• Adopt the founder's mindset: build the thing to outgrow you
  • See why capital is not your real constraint, and what is
  • Read the market context: demographics, capital flows and the execution gap
  • Apply the four levers of scale: operations, growth drivers, insight and incentives
  • Recognise the levels of entrepreneurship and the valley where scale dies
  • Lead yourself first, then build people who carry the vision

steps.title: Earn the right to be offended

item.content:
It is not about ideas. It is about making ideas happen.

Vusi opens with a challenge: ideas are cheap, and growth begins when your thinking is challenged. His one mandate for this session is to offend you, because offence means either you care, or you have believed something that needs to change.

In this lesson

  • Why ideas alone are worthless without execution
  • The privilege of being offended and challenged
  • How to show up ready to rethink what you know

Vusi funded his own thesis when no institution would, then spent a decade proving it through My Growth Fund and the School of Scale.

In this lesson

  • Why the founders who scaled were never superhuman
  • The real question: what did they know that others did not
  • Why the African story is strong everywhere except business
  • How the 154 fund backs family businesses in transition

The two words at the centre of the talk: founder's mindset.

In this lesson

  • Why not every business owner, entrepreneur or leader is a founder
  • The defining trait: founders build the thing to outgrow them
  • What it means to build intentionally, beyond yourself

steps.title: Capital isn't the problem, you are

item.content:
A numbers-driven case: there is more capital looking to back founders than there are founders building.

In this lesson

  • Why, if you are not attracting capital, the problem is you
  • How M&A deals grew from 40,000 a year to about 60,000
  • The flood of money: half of all US dollars ever, printed in five years

Legacies are not hoped for, they are built, and building starts with understanding your context.

In this lesson

  • The roughly one trillion dollar opportunity across Africa's top markets
  • Why sub-Saharan Africa is the world's largest growth opportunity
  • The youngest population on earth, and the execution gap

steps.title: Play the game you are gifted

item.content:
In a decade the world's largest companies flipped to technology. So where does Africa's growth come from?

In this lesson

  • How the global top 10 went from three to eight tech firms
  • Why Africa should play the game it has been gifted
  • The rule that capital follows scale

steps.title: The four things you need to scale

item.content:
The data points to four things that separate businesses that scale.

The four things

  • Synthesise your operations so work continues without you
  • Implement your three growth drivers and cut the noise
  • Move from instinct to insight
  • Align incentives across your people

How Vusi runs a global team whose incentives are aligned with his, so a keynote gets built without him in the room.

In this lesson

  • Tie incentives directly to your business objectives
  • Let clients score the work, and let bonuses follow the scores
  • How sales scripts and simple rules scale one founder everywhere

There are levels to this, and most owners get stuck long before they become founders.

The levels

  • Level 1, the professional: if you stop, the work stops
  • Level 2, self-employed: can you take 90 days away
  • Level 3, the business owner: you write down the rules and the code

steps.title: The valley where scale goes to die

item.content:
Implementing the rules is where reality slaps your spreadsheet back.

In this lesson

  • Why your Excel assumptions do not survive the real world
  • Implementation fatigue, and falling out of love and into life
  • Why 90 percent retreat, and how the 10 percent push through
  • Business equals problems: identify them, do not just fix them

Founders plant a vision and build the people who make it true.

In this lesson

  • Grow people who carry the vision forward
  • Leadership is a mirror: lead yourself before you lead others
  • Know your founder DNA across six areas of development
